extracted.intended_audience: applicants and patent practitioners preparing and filing a demand for international preliminary examination (PCT Chapter II)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and formal requirements for preparing and filing a demand for international preliminary examination under the PCT (Chapter II), including statements on amendments, languages, fees, signatures, supporting documents, timings, and substantive examination criteria (novelty, inventive step, industrial applicability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to amend before and during international preliminary examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant has the right, under Article 34(2)(b), to amend the claims, the description and the drawings before the start of the international preliminary examination and also during the examination, if time permits, until the preparation of the international preliminary report on patentability (Chapter II of the PCT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is effectively a second opportunity for amending claims (first opportunity: Article 19 amendments to the International Bureau). For further details refer to specified paragraphs. Amendments under Article 34 should be submitted with, and attached to, the demand if they are to be taken into account at the start of the IPE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete the statement concerning amendments (Box IV)
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement concerning amendments should be completed since it enables the IPEA to identify which documents will serve as the basis for the start of the international preliminary examination and to start it as soon as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to complete the statement correctly is not fatal, but omission may delay the start of the IPE or leave insufficient time for intended amendments to be taken into account. If no amendments are filed and none are intended, the IPE will start on the basis of the application as filed. If amendments exist but are not indicated, the start may be delayed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indication of language for international preliminary examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Completing the indication of the language for the purposes of the IPE and its associated check-boxes helps the IPEA determine quickly whether the demand and international application are in a language accepted by that Authority or whether a translation is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also helps decide whether amendments filed with the demand are in the appropriate language. Complete these boxes to avoid delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to mark Box IV check-boxes for description/claims/drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Under item (1) the applicant must indicate whether the IPEA should start on the basis of the international application as originally filed or on the basis of parts (description, claims, drawings) as amended under Article 19 or Article 34.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark check-boxes only where the applicant wishes amendments to be taken into account for the start of the IPE. If Article 19 amendments are to be taken into account, attach a copy of them and any accompanying statement to the demand; if a check-box is marked but the documents are missing, the start of IPE will be delayed until the IPEA receives them. Amendments under Article 34 should be submitted with and attached to the demand and the appropriate check-boxes marked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking checkbox to consider Article 19 amendments reversed
rubrics_metrics.description: Box IV item '2. The applicant wishes any amendments to the claims made under Article 19 to be considered as reversed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark this only where the applicant previously made Article 19 amendments but no longer wishes them to be considered for IPE; marking has the effect of considering those amendments reversed by an amendment under Article 34.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request to postpone start of IPE where Article 19 time limit not expired
rubrics_metrics.description: Box IV item '3. Where the IPEA wishes to start the IPE at the same time as the international search in accordance with Rule 69.1(b), the applicant requests the IPEA to postpone the start of the IPE until the expiration of the applicable time limit under Rule 69.1(d)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark only where, at time of filing the demand, the time limit for filing Article 19 amendments has not expired and the applicant intends to file such amendments after filing the demand (typically when demand filed before ISR is available). If later no amendments are filed, the applicant should notify the IPEA so the IPE can start.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request to postpone start of IPE until Rule 54bis.1(a) expiry
rubrics_metrics.description: Box IV item '4. The applicant expressly requests to postpone the start of the IPE until the expiration of the applicable time limit under Rule 54bis.1(a).'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark this if the applicant wishes to postpone start until that time; otherwise, where ISA and IPEA are different, examination will commence once IPEA has required fees and ISR/written opinion or declaration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple check-boxes may be marked
rubrics_metrics.description: Several check-boxes in Box IV may be marked simultaneously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: applicant may have filed Article 19 amendments and also wish Article 34 amendments to description and/or drawings to be taken into account, possibly with further Article 34 amendments to the already amended claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant may file further amendments during IPE (statement not binding)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant is not precluded from later making amendments, or further amendments, during the course of the IPE regardless of what appears in the statement concerning amendments; the statement is not binding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, the statement is used by the IPEA to determine when and on what basis the IPE starts. Amendments/arguments received after the IPEA has begun to draw up the report may not be taken into account. Applicants should be definite at filing time about the basis for IPE; if intending Article 34 amendments but unable to submit them with the demand, mention the intention in a letter with the demand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election of States by filing a demand
rubrics_metrics.description: The making of a demand has the effect of electing all Contracting States which have been designated and which are bound by Chapter II of the PCT (usually all except Uruguay).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is automatic when the demand is filed; check Annexes/Rules for exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and completion of the Check List (Box VI)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Check List in Box VI should be completed to allow the IPEA to verify the completeness of documents filed with the demand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indications in the Check List (notably relating to amendments) should correspond with Box IV indications. Complete it accurately to avoid inconsistencies and delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirements for the demand
rubrics_metrics.description: The demand must be signed by the applicant or, if more than one applicant, by all the applicants making the demand (i.e., the applicants for the States elected). An agent or common representative may sign on behalf of the applicant(s) who appointed him/her.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A common agent or deemed common representative may sign on behalf of all. If one or more applicants' signatures are missing, the IPEA will not invite applicants to furnish the missing signatures provided at least one applicant has signed. A notice of withdrawal must be signed by applicant(s) or an authorized agent as specified by the Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of seal instead of signature (where permitted)
rubrics_metrics.description: In certain Offices (e.g., CNIPA, MOIP Republic of Korea) a seal may be used instead of a signature in the demand or other papers filed with that Office as IPEA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In specific cases (e.g., demand filed in English with EPO as IPEA for applications filed with JPO as receiving Office) a signature must be furnished instead of a seal. Follow the receiving/IPEA Office rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notes to the demand form are guidance only
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notes to the demand form indicate, in relation to each Box, what indications are required and how they are to be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes are intended to facilitate completion and are not required to be filed with the demand. Refer to the WIPO link for the Notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the fee calculation sheet (recommended)
rubrics_metrics.description: The fee calculation sheet helps the applicant calculate total fees payable to the IPEA; usually annexed to the printed demand form but not part of the form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Its use is not mandatory but strongly recommended to help the IPEA verify calculations and identify errors. Refer to the Notes to the fee calculation sheet for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees payable with the demand (preliminary examination fee and handling fee)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two kinds of fees are payable in connection with the demand: (i) the preliminary examination fee (fixed by and accrues to the IPEA) and (ii) the handling fee (fixed in Schedule of Fees and accrues to the International Bureau).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the only fees payable for filing a demand (there is no separate 'election fee'). See Annex E and Rules for amounts and particulars.

rubrics_metrics.name: To whom and in what currency fees are payable
rubrics_metrics.description: The preliminary examination fee and the handling fee are payable to the IPEA, which forwards the handling fee to the International Bureau. Fees are generally payable in the currency or one of the currencies prescribed by the IPEA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete information on currency and specific payment instructions is in Annex E (and specific IPEA instructions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and conditions of fee reductions
rubrics_metrics.description: Some IPEAs offer reductions of their preliminary examination fee; in addition, a 90% reduction of the handling fee is available if (a) the applicant is a natural person and a national of and resides in a State meeting specified GDP and filing thresholds, or (b) the applicant is a national of and resides in a least developed country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If several applicants, each must satisfy criteria. Applicant must be true and only owner and not under obligation to assign rights to a non-eligible party to obtain handling fee reduction. Eligibility based on Box II indications; no separate request required. Refer to WIPO link for list of eligible States and Annexes for country-specific reductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: When fees are due and consequences of non-payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary examination fee and handling fee must be paid within one month from the date the demand was submitted or 22 months from the priority date, whichever expires later (or within one month from receipt by the competent IPEA where transmitted under Rule 59.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequences of non-payment or late payment are described elsewhere; late payment may incur late fee; payment time limits differ for form/language corrections vs. fee payment corrections (no extension for fee payment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Refunds of fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPEA will refund the handling fee if the demand is withdrawn before being sent to the International Bureau or if the demand is considered not to have been submitted because none of the applicants had the right to file a demand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each IPEA decides at its discretion whether to refund the preliminary examination fee (or part thereof) in other circumstances; details in Annex E.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPEA processing of demand and correction invitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPEA promptly notifies the applicant of the date of receipt of the demand and examines the demand to ascertain whether it meets all requirements; if not, the IPEA invites the applicant to comply and correct defects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invitations for defects as to form or language specify a time limit of at least one month (may be extended); invitations for fee payment defects specify one month with no extension (late payment fee may be required). Payment is considered received if received by IPEA before expiration of applicable time limit or before declaration that the demand is not submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences if applicant complies or fails to comply with invitation
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant complies within the specified time limit there is no adverse consequence other than possible delay, except where the defect prevented identification of the international application (in that case the demand is considered received on date of correction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If after expiration of time limit a required signature or other indication is still lacking, the demand is considered not to have been submitted and the IPEA will so declare.

rubrics_metrics.name: When the international preliminary examination starts
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to exceptions, the IPEA starts the IPE when it is in possession of the demand, the amount due (in full) for the handling fee and preliminary examination fee (including any late fee), and either the international search report and the written opinion established under Rule 43bis.1 or a declaration by the ISA that no ISR will be established and the written opinion, unless the applicant expressly requests postponement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delays can occur if indicated amendments require the IPEA to wait for copies or translations before starting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telescoped procedure (simultaneous start of ISR and IPE)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the competent IPEA is part of the same Office as the competent ISA, the IPE may, if the Office wishes and unless the applicant requested postponement, start at the same time as the international search (telescoped procedure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant can request postponement to avoid telescoping (see Box IV options).

rubrics_metrics.name: IPEA will not start IPE until Article 19 amendments (indicated to be taken into account) are received
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the statement indicates that Article 19 amendments are to be taken into account, the IPEA will not start the IPE before it has received a copy of the amendments and accompanying letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach copies to the demand to allow maximum time. The International Bureau will send copies if IPEA hasn't received them, but waiting for those copies may delay the start.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to postpone the start of IPE (Box IV indication)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the statement indicates postponement, the IPEA will not start the IPE before the earliest of: (i) receipt of a copy of Article 19 amendments; (ii) receipt of a notice that the applicant does not intend to make Article 19 amendments; or (iii) expiration of the applicable time limit under Rule 46.1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants who indicate postponement should promptly inform the IPEA of any amendments or decision not to file amendments to gain maximum time for IPE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and translation requirements for amendments filed with the demand
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the statement indicates Article 34 amendments are submitted with the demand but none are actually submitted, the IPEA will not start before receiving them or inviting applicant to file them and expiry of that invitation; any Article 34 amendments and accompanying letters must be in the language of publication or in the language of the translation used for IPE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If amendments are filed in another language, a translation into the language in which IPE is carried out must be furnished. If not in required language, the IPEA will invite translation within a reasonable time; failure to furnish translations within the time limit means the IPEA will not take the amendments into account for IPE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority document and translation may be requested by IPEA
rubrics_metrics.description: If the IPEA needs a copy of a claimed priority application and the IB already has it, the IB furnishes a copy on request; if applicant failed to provide the priority document under Rule 17.1 the IPRP may be established as if the priority had not been claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No elected Office may later disregard the priority claim without giving the applicant opportunity to furnish the priority document within a reasonable time. If the priority document is in another language and IPEA considers validity of the claim relevant, the IPEA may invite a translation to be furnished within two months or the IPRP may be established as if the priority was not claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the international preliminary examination (substantive scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of the IPE is to formulate a preliminary and non‑binding opinion on whether the claimed invention appears (i) to be novel, (ii) to involve an inventive step (to be non‑obvious), and (iii) to be industrially applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The IPRP gives a good indication of likely results in the national phase, although national laws differ in approach to these criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of novelty for IPE purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: For IPE purposes, a claimed invention is considered novel if it is not anticipated by the prior art. Rule 64 defines prior art for the purposes of examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Rule 64's definition of prior art when assessing novelty during IPE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of inventive step for IPE purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: For IPE purposes, a claimed invention is considered to involve an inventive step if, having regard to prior art as defined in the Regulations, it is not, at the prescribed relevant date, obvious to a person skilled in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Rule 65 for further details on how to apply the inventive step/non-obviousness standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of industrial applicability for IPE purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: For IPE purposes, a claimed invention is considered industrially applicable if, according to its nature, it can be made or used (in the technological sense) in any kind of industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply this practical/technological standard when assessing industrial applicability during IPE.
